cells.tense: Right now you are settling accounts as you go, and you hold the pen.
cells.ask: Before a yes today, check it against what it costs you, and answer from that, not from the moment.
cells.core:
You keep things level without keeping score. When something gets lopsided, you feel it early and you adjust it early, and people come away feeling treated well without being able to say why. That adjustment is quiet and constant, and it is one of the things people trust most in you.

The other half is that you are near the end of something and free of it. What you finished holds together, and it still holds. Balance like this does not stand still; you keep it by noticing what has shifted. So pay attention to the next adjustment you make, and let it count as the work it is.
cells.sheetLine: You keep things level without keeping score.
cells.verb: recalibrating what has fallen out of proportion
cells.place: the doorway where what you finished becomes what you start

cells.tense: You are standing in a future where the reckoning has already happened.
cells.ask: Leave one account today without adding to it. Name what is owed you, then put it down and hold it. Do not collect and do not cross it off.
cells.core:
Somewhere ahead of you, the imbalance has been tallied. So you are tracking constantly — what you gave, what came back, what is still owed. It is not greed. You are bracing. The running total feels like the only thing that will keep the field level when the reckoning arrives.

What that costs is the give and take itself. When a gift turns into an entry, the exchange stops moving. You can hold a hard thing steady without forcing it; put that toward what you are waiting on. Name the debt once, then leave it alone for a while. What is not carried does not have to come out even.
cells.sheetLine: The tally is taking the place of the exchange.
cells.verb: recalibrating what has fallen out of proportion

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are owed and say it plainly today — one sentence, no argument, no apology — and keep your own yes or no to tonight.
cells.core:
You have stopped claiming what is yours. Not because you do not see it — you see the imbalance — but because asking has felt like it costs more than the loss. So the unfair thing stands, and you call that being easygoing. The weighing itself is not broken. You are just not using it on your own behalf.

Something is finished and you have not stepped out of it. Stepping out means taking up space again. Small practice helps here: repeat one act of asking until it stops being an event. Claim one thing, badly, before you are ready. The fairness you have been giving away to keep things calm is yours to hold.
cells.sheetLine: You see what is owed and you are not asking for it.

cells.tense: The scales are running under the conversation, and you have not signed for them.
cells.ask: Say out loud the next small thing that bothers you, before it gains weight — one sentence, to one person or to yourself.
cells.core:
Being fair is usually automatic in you. You read a room and adjust without deciding to, and most of the time the adjustment is right. Nothing has to be added up for that to work; it just lands.

Underneath it now, something is being weighed that you would not call a count, and it shapes what you say next without showing in what you say. Nobody around you can see the totals, and you have not signed for them. The fix is not balancing an account. It is knowing what you attend to. Say the small thing when it appears, before it gains weight, and it stays information instead of a debt.
cells.sheetLine: You are keeping a count you do not know you are keeping.
